text:
violet: FYI - getting reports of sustained p99/p999 latency increases for several Dedicated GPU pools in apac-southeast1 since ~02:10 UTC. A subset of large-model (8k+) jobs are timing out or being retried. Impact: ~4% of Dedicated requests, most pronounced on reserved GPU pools with burst tenants. investigating. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Status page created: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/3316543210 investigating
samar: Oncall. Looking at node telemetry and provider event stream. I’m seeing a spike in preemption/eviction events for a cluster of host VMs between 02:05-02:18 UTC. Could be noisy-neighbor spot churn.
leo: Correlating scheduler logs - concurrent GPU reclaim events triggered multiple reschedules, causing long kotlin-worker stall and model kernel recompile thrash. That explains the p99 spike and job timeouts.
nisha: Kicking off targeted mitigation: cordon affected hosts and shift active serving slices to reserved-capacity pools. Starting automated drain now. ETA ~6-9m for initial shift.
ops-bot: Drain job started on apac-gpu-pool-3 at 02:22UTC (job id: drain-3316). Reserving 40% capacity in apac-reserved-01 for failover.
cory: Can we enable preemption-aware scheduling flag (fair_preempt_v2) for apac pools to reduce reschedule churn? If safe, I’ll flip and watch for regressions.
samar: Agreed. Enabling fair_preempt_v2 on a single edge-slice for canary now.
ops-bot: fair_preempt_v2 enabled on apac-slice-7 at 02:26UTC. Observability: reschedule rate down 63% on that slice vs baseline.
leo: After drain and failover, tail latency dropped ~85% from peak. Error retries for long-context jobs decreased significantly. Current user-facing impact estimated <0.3% of Dedicated requests.
violet: Publishing interim note to status page and alerting affected customers. Internal runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/dedicated-preemptions
incident-bot: Public status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/3316543210 mitigated (partial). Next update scheduled in 30m or on material change.
nisha: Post-mitigation: planning follow-ups - (1) tighten host selection filters to avoid spot heavy racks, (2) add proactive drain on provider preemption signals, (3) capacity reservation heuristics for large-model jobs.
cory: Also recommend adding a transient retry budget for long-context requests so short transient preemptions don't surface as customer errors.
samar: Good notes. We'll run a post-incident triage and RCA. Tentative RCA timeline: initial draft in 48 hours, final postmortem within 7 days.
violet: Thanks team. If you see any anomalies or customer escalations, post here and tag @samar. Publishing customer comms now and escalating to Account Execs for top-impacted tenants. :white_check_mark:
